content.title: About
content.content: Plain baby toddler yogurt is a gentle dairy product made from whole cow's milk without added sugar, flavorings, or colorants. It contains live cultures of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium that support a healthy gut microbiome and is suitable for children from 6 months old.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The yogurt provides probiotics that help strengthen a child's immune system.
Plain yogurt is often one of the first dairy foods introduced when transitioning from breast milk to solid foods.
Unlike fruit‑flavored yogurts, plain versions contain no added sugar, making them kinder to young teeth.
The natural acidity of yogurt enhances calcium and phosphorus absorption.
Enzymes in yogurt partially break down lactose, making it easier to digest for children with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Live cultures promote the growth of beneficial bacteria, improving digestion and immunity.

items.title: Source of calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Calcium is essential for bone and tooth development, while vitamin D aids its absorption.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Protein supports muscle growth and overall development in toddlers.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Absence of added sugars helps avoid rapid blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Fermentation enzymes partially break down lactose, making the product more tolerable for children with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some children may be allergic to casein or whey, causing skin reactions or digestive issues.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Kids with pronounced lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming yogurt.

items.title: Shelf‑life monitoring
items.content: Yogurt spoils quickly if not stored properly; always consume before the printed date.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improper handling after opening can allow pathogenic bacteria to grow.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve 50–100 ml portions from a clean spoon. It can be mixed with fruit or vegetable purees or stirred into oatmeal for variety. Do not add sugar or honey for children under one year.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the yogurt refrigerated at 2–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 2–3 days and do not leave it at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

burrito-beef-with-beans-and-rice-cheese.title: Burrito, beef, with beans and rice, cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A burrito with beef, beans, rice and cheese is a classic Mexican dish consisting of a large soft wheat tortilla filled with sautéed beef, cooked beans, fluffy rice and melted cheese. The dish is popular worldwide for its rich flavor, convenience and the ability to customize the fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour was more available than corn.
Traditional beef is seasoned with cumin, paprika, chili and garlic, giving it a distinctive aroma.
Black or pinto beans are commonly used, providing protein and fiber.
Mexican‑style rice is often cooked with tomato paste and turmeric, giving it a golden hue.
Cheese such as cheddar or Mexican “queso” melts smoothly and binds the other ingredients.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Beef and beans supply complete amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Beans and rice provide dietary fiber that promotes digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef offers heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese adds calcium and a modest amount of vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: Carbohydrates from rice and fats from cheese give lasting satiety and fuel for active days.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Cheese and certain cuts of beef can be high in saturated fat, so people with heart disease should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Seasonings and cheese add salt, which may be a concern for those with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Burritos are calorie‑dense; overconsumption may lead to weight gain if eaten frequently.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are hand‑held, but they can also be sliced in half and served with salsa, guacamole or sour cream. For a lighter version, substitute part of the beef with turkey or add extra vegetables such as tomatoes, avocado or lettuce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For freezing, wrap tightly in plastic film and place in a freezer bag – it keeps well for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to ensure the filling is evenly hot.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate cookie with rice cereal is a crunchy snack that combines sweet chocolate, a tender dough, and the light airy texture of rice cereal. It works well as a quick bite, a dessert component, or a simple treat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice cereal gives the cookie a distinctive snap and makes it less dense than traditional chocolate cookies.
Dark chocolate (70% cacao) is often used for a richer flavor and added health benefits.
The cookie is popular at children's parties because it breaks easily into bite‑size pieces.
The chocolate‑rice combination is common in Asian cuisine, where rice is considered a “golden” ingredient.

items.title: Antioxidant source
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Cocoa powder provides a good amount of non‑heme iron.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from rice cereal are quickly absorbed, giving a rapid energy lift.

items.title: Magnesium content
items.content: Magnesium in cocoa supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When prepared correctly, the recipe contains no hydrogenated oils.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The dough usually contains wheat flour, which can be problematic for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Chocolate cookies are typically sweet, so those monitoring blood sugar should watch portion size.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Dark chocolate contains a small amount of caffeine, which may affect caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Large cookie pieces can pose a choking risk for young kids.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie as a stand‑alone snack, crumble it into ice cream or yogurt, or use it as a base for dessert tartlets. For a softer texture, warm it briefly in the microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to maintain crunchiness and prevent mold growth.

content.title: About
content.content: Dark chocolate candy with nuts consists of bite‑size pieces of high‑cocoa dark chocolate (usually 70 % cocoa or more) that contain whole or chopped nuts such as almonds, hazelnuts, cashews or peanuts. The candy offers a rich, slightly bitter chocolate flavor complemented by the crunchy texture of the nuts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark chocolate contains more antioxidants than milk chocolate thanks to its high flavonoid content.
Nuts add not only flavor but also healthy fats, protein, and minerals.
The first recipes for dark chocolate with nuts appeared in Europe in the 19th century.
Cocoa butter in dark chocolate stabilizes aroma and extends shelf life.
These candies are often used as a quick energy boost by athletes.

items.title: Rich in flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids in dark chocolate help reduce oxidative stress and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium from cocoa and nuts supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Nuts provide monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for the heart.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Dark chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, improving mood.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Nuts add fiber, which aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: The candy can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to nuts.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Combined dark chocolate and nuts make the product calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Cocoa contains small amounts of caffeine, which may affect sleep if consumed in large quantities.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Some versions contain added sugar, which should be considered by people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candy as a standalone snack, stir into yogurt or granola, or use in baking. It can also be gently melted and drizzled over ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent chocolate bloom.

fruit-flavored-drink-with-high-vitamin-c.title: Fruit Flavored Drink with High Vitamin C, Diet

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit flavored drink with high vitamin C is a non‑alcoholic refreshing beverage enriched with vitamin C, low in calories and suitable for diet nutrition. It is made from natural fruit extracts, sweetened with low‑calorie sweeteners and contains minimal sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vitamin C in the drink helps support the immune system.
Low‑calorie formulation makes it popular among weight‑conscious consumers.
Often fortified with additional B‑vitamins to boost energy levels.
Natural flavorings keep the taste bright and authentic.
Usually packaged in recyclable glass or plastic containers.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress and supports normal immune function.

items.title: Calorie‑controlled diet
items.content: Low sugar and calorie content make the drink suitable for diet plans and weight management.

items.title: Improved hydration
items.content: The liquid base helps maintain the body’s water balance, especially in warm weather.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Vitamin C contributes to collagen synthesis, promoting skin elasticity and a healthy appearance.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Added B‑vitamins aid in converting food into energy, reducing feelings of fatigue.

items.title: Allergy to fruit components
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific fruit extracts used in the drink.

items.title: Excessive vitamin C intake
items.content: Very high amounts of vitamin C can cause gastrointestinal discomfort such as diarrhea.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Large doses of vitamin C may affect the efficacy of certain drugs, for example anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Consume
content.content: Drink chilled, preferably throughout the day. It can be added to smoothies or used as a base for non‑alcoholic cocktails.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Hard salted pretzel sticks coated with dark chocolate. They feature a crunchy texture, a slightly sweet chocolate shell and the classic salty pretzel flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hard pretzels originate from Germany, where they are known as "Brezeln".
Chocolate coating extends shelf life by protecting the dry pretzel from moisture.
The salty‑sweet contrast is one of the most popular flavor pairings in snack foods.
Pretzels are commonly served at sporting events and movie theaters as a quick bite.
During the 2020s there has been a noticeable rise in demand for chocolate‑covered versions of traditional pretzels.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: The wheat‑based hard pretzel provides slow‑release energy from complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Both wheat flour and cocoa powder contribute modest amounts of iron, supporting blood formation.

items.title: Mood support
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin and endorphin production, improving mood.

items.title: Magnesium content
items.content: Magnesium in chocolate aids normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat‑based pretzel can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The chocolate coating adds sugar, so the snack should be consumed in moderation, especially by individuals with diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Both the hard pretzel and chocolate make the product energy‑dense; large portions may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Dark chocolate contains small amounts of caffeine, which may affect caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels are convenient as a stand‑alone snack, paired with coffee, tea or milk. They can be added to dessert platters, used as a garnish for ice cream, or incorporated into recipes that call for a crunchy sweet‑salty element.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer storage, keep refrigerated to prevent the chocolate from melting and losing its crunch. Discard if the pretzels become soft, develop off‑odors, or show any mold.

content.title: About
content.content: Raisins are dried grapes obtained through natural or artificial drying. Their sweet, concentrated flavor and soft chewable texture make them a popular ingredient in baked goods, desserts, and snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Raisins are made from various grape varieties, including white, red, and black grapes.
Drying preserves almost all the nutrients of fresh grapes, but in a more concentrated form.
In ancient cultures, raisins were used as an energy source for travelers and warriors.
Raisins are commonly added to traditional dishes worldwide, such as pilaf, kutia, and Christmas cookies.
Golden raisins are produced from grapes with high sugar content, giving them a bright golden color after drying.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Raisins contain polyphenols and flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports normal digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Raisins provide a good plant-based source of iron, useful for preventing anemia.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in raisins help regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Natural sugars (glucose and fructose) are rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate energy lift.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Raisins contain a lot of natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Raisins are calorie-dense, so they should be consumed in moderation on weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Sulfites
items.content: Some manufacturers add sulfites to preserve color; they can cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Risk of tooth decay
items.content: Sticky texture and high sugar levels can promote cavities if oral hygiene is not maintained.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raisins can be enjoyed as a snack, added to granola, yogurt, salads, baked goods, sauces, and marinades. They are also used to make compotes and infused drinks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raisins in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For long‑term storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth.
